claim: NullPropagatedOperands descends into SqlBinaryExpression operands for every operator type, but AndAlso/OrElse do not propagate NULL under three-valued logic (NULL AND FALSE = FALSE, NULL OR TRUE = TRUE); DropNotNullChecks therefore deletes the IS NOT NULL guard around a logical-operator result and CASE WHEN x IS NOT NULL THEN (x OR y) ELSE NULL END collapses to x OR y, returning TRUE/FALSE instead of NULL and changing the row set in WHERE. Reachable via EF's own null-semantics compensation (a == b -> a = b AND b IS NOT NULL). Verified by executing queries at HEAD vs parent commit on SQLite against a LINQ-to-Objects oracle.
raw: #1 🔴 Critical: `NullPropagatedOperands` treats `AndAlso`/`OrElse` operands as null-propagating; queries return wrong values and wrong rows

claim: When the collapsed CASE result is a boolean search condition (e.g. a plain Equal comparison), SQL Server's search-condition converter materializes it as CASE WHEN <pred> THEN CAST(1 AS bit) ELSE CAST(0 AS bit) END, folding UNKNOWN into false; the deleted outer CASE ... ELSE NULL END was the only thing preserving NULL, so a bool? projection like x.NullableIntA != null ? (bool?)(x.NullableIntA == x.Id) : null returns false instead of null on SQL Server. Distinct from #1; SQLite is unaffected so the Sqlite functional tests cannot see it. Verified via ToQueryString at both commits.
raw: #2 🔴 Critical: dropping the guard around a boolean *search-condition* result loses `NULL`, because `UNKNOWN` materializes as `false`
